page.layout: One printed page (240) with running text in one column; narrow notes in the left margin, Greek note at the foot of the margin. Right of the page, the edge of the neighbouring page (not transcribed).

main_text.p: ut fiant cùm privatim, tùm vel maximè in publicis cœtibus, (sic enim, cum optimis quibusque interpretibus, hunc locum intelligendum exiftimo,) obtestationes, preces, postulationes, & gratiarum actiones: ut pro omnibus in universum hominibus primò (ex intuitu Charitatis, & in ordine ad finem spiritualem, felicitatem scil. æternam in vita futura,) in quantum sunt omnes homines, aut actu, aut saltem potestate, membra Corporis Christi Mystici; ita pro Regibus aliisque supremâ potestate prædítis in specie (ex intuitu etiam Prudentiæ & in ordine ad finem Temporalem, felicitatem scil. externam in vita præsenti,) in quantum sunt præcipua membra Corporis Politici. A quorum potestate, Lativâ Legum & Executivâ, prout utraque rectè aut secus administraverint, plurimùm pendet reliquorum membrorum, adeóque totius corporis, vel felicitas summa, vel summa infelicitas. Proinde quum fit Legum-latio, ut jam ante dixi-mus, Suprema Jurisdictionis Politica actus præcipua: qui est supremæ illius Jurisdictionis totiusque Politici Regiminis, idem est & Legum ferendarum supremus Finis; bonum scil. Communitatis. Proba-tur secundò, à natura Finis, quasi demonstratione priori. Is est rei cujusque Finis in suo ordine ultimus, ad quem omnes illius rei actus reducuntur, tanquam ad primum principium sui regulativum; & ad quem referuntur, tanquam ad id cujus gratiâ ultimatè fiunt: unde causa Finalis Aristoteli τὸ οὗ ἕνεκα[?] appellatur. Sed omnes ᾿Οι νόμο-[?] δίκαι[?]α εἶναι φασὶ τὸ κοινῇ συμφέρον[?] [illegible, ~6 letters] Ἀριστο-[?] 8. Ethic II{*} Legum actiones a Bono Communi regulantur tanquam a primo fine Principio & Canone; & ad Bonum Commune referuntur, tanquam ad ultimum id cujus gratiâ fiunt: ut patet discurrendo per singulos actus: ergo, &c. Quorsum enim res, aut bonæ præcipiuntur, aut malæ vetantur, aut permittuntur mediæ & neutræ. Aut quorsum hominibus, vel de Rep. bene me[?]

page.notes: Printed in the left margin beside the line "tur fecundo": a section mark "2." (in the paragraph, beside "Proba-tur secundò"). This is a margin note; it is included as text of the paragraph's left-margin note in the marked position: 2. Left-margin Greek note (beside "Sed omnes"): lines are very faint; Greek letters in the margin and in the text (τὸ οὗ ἕνεκα, the note's Greek lines) are doubtful and marked [?]. The margin ends with "Aristo." and "8. Ethic II"; the order of the Greek lines is uncertain. The text is cut off at "bene me" at the foot of the page; the word is not clearly readable and is marked [?]. The right edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page (tis, cor, trif, illi ...) and is not transcribed. A faint mark at the foot of the page ("s. R") and show-through below the text were judged unreliable and are not transcribed as signature. Italic type is judged from the scan; some italic/roman boundaries (e.g. "Corporis Politici", "fupremus Finis") are uncertain.
